title: fix(auth): TOTP enrollment names the deployment app name as its issuer, not Better Auth
body:
Fixes #21731

Clause-②: no

A TOTP enrollment now names the deployment, not the auth library. `/two-factor/enable` and `/two-factor/get-totp-uri` answered `otpauth://totp/Better%20Auth:...&issuer=Better+Auth`. They now carry the deployment's app name: `OS_APP_NAME`, else the configured app name, else `ObjectStack`. An explicitly set `branding.workspace_name` still outranks it. Existing enrollments keep working, because the issuer is a display label beside an unchanged secret.

## What changed

- **`@objectstack/plugin-auth`.** `AuthManager.createAuthInstance()` passes `getAppName()` to better-auth as its `appName`. That is the one app-name authority every auth email already reads. No second read was added, and `twoFactor({ issuer })` is left unset (see the better-auth reading below).
- **`@objectstack/cli` (producer side).** `objectstack serve` constructs `AuthPlugin` with `appName: resolveDeploymentAppName(...)`. `resolveDeploymentAppName` is the email capability's existing chain (`OS_APP_NAME` > `config.email.appName` > `config.email.defaultTemplateContext.appName` > `config.appName` > `ObjectStack`), factored out of `resolveEmailCapabilityArg` unchanged. Both consumers now call that one resolver with the same arguments.
- **Docs.** The `OS_APP_NAME` row in `content/docs/deployment/environment-variables.mdx` now says what the variable names. It used to say "the OAuth app display name", which was never true.
- **Changeset.** `.changeset/21731-totp-issuer-app-name.md`, `patch` for both packages. It says that an existing enrollment keeps working.

## Why the landing reaches `packages/cli`: the triage premise was false under `serve`

The card and triage both assumed that `getAppName()` honours `OS_APP_NAME`. Under `objectstack serve` it did not. `serve` built `AuthPlugin` with no `appName`, so `getAppName()` answered `ObjectStack`. Auth emails hid this: their own `appName` outranks the email service's template context (`plugin-email/src/email-service.ts`, the `{ ...defaultTemplateContext, ...input.data }` merge), and the template context was the only place that carried `OS_APP_NAME`.

These readings come from the public door, an `os dev` boot (`pnpm dev:todo -- --fresh`, `OS_AUTH_TWO_FACTOR=true`, `OS_APP_NAME='Acme Ops'`, seeded admin, secrets redacted):

| build | `POST /api/v1/auth/two-factor/enable` totpURI | password-reset email subject (`sys_email`) |
|---|---|---|
| the `serve.ts` line ablated, `auth-manager.ts` fix in place | `otpauth://totp/ObjectStack:admin%40objectos.ai?...&issuer=ObjectStack` | `Reset your ObjectStack password` |
| this PR | `otpauth://totp/Acme%20Ops:admin%40objectos.ai?...&issuer=Acme+Ops` | (see the liveness table) |

Without the `serve` half, the card's first pin (the issuer equals `OS_APP_NAME`) fails at the public door. The same root cause also fixes the auth emails' `{{appName}}` under `serve`.

## better-auth 1.7.3, read off its dist

- `appName` is read once, at init: `dist/context/create-context.mjs:131`, `appName: options.appName || "Better Auth"`.
- That context value is read in exactly two places, both otpauth URIs:
  - `dist/plugins/two-factor/index.mjs:170` (enable): `issuer || options?.issuer || ctx.context.appName`. The first term is the request body's own `issuer`.
  - `dist/plugins/two-factor/totp/index.mjs:133` (get-totp-uri): `options?.issuer || ctx.context.appName`. Here `options` is `totpOptions`, and its type omits `issuer` (`dist/plugins/two-factor/types.d.mts:25` declares `totpOptions` as `TOTPOptions` with `issuer` omitted).
- No other runtime read of `appName` exists in `better-auth`, `@better-auth/core`, `sso`, `scim`, `oauth-provider`, `telemetry` or `kysely-adapter`. `core` has 3 hits and all of them are `.d.mts` docs. The other packages have 0.
- **No stored or wire identifier changes.** The cookie prefix is the literal `"better-auth"` (`dist/cookies/index.mjs:28`). The core type doc says the prefix defaults from `appName`, but in 1.7.3 it does not. better-auth reads no `APP_NAME` env either.
- So `appName` is the one typed key that names both routes. `twoFactor({ issuer })` alone would leave `get-totp-uri` on `Better Auth`, so the triage condition for setting it explicitly does not hold.

## Liveness: what follows a branding change

| reading (public door) | result |
|---|---|
| boot with `OS_BRANDING_WORKSPACE_NAME='Env Brand'` and `OS_APP_NAME='Acme Ops'`, first enable | `issuer=Env+Brand`: the boot-time branding value reaches the issuer |
| after boot, `PUT /api/settings/branding {"workspace_name":"Renamed Co"}` (200), then enable and get-totp-uri | both still `issuer=Acme+Ops` |
| same process, password-reset email | subject `Reset your Renamed Co password` |

`ctx.context.appName` is fixed when the better-auth instance is built. A rename after that reaches the issuer at the next rebuild (a restart, or an auth-settings change that calls `applyConfigPatch`). Auth emails follow it on the next send. No route in `auth-manager.ts` follows the live value on both TOTP routes without rebuilding the instance: a getter-backed `twoFactor({ issuer })` would follow it on `enable` only. The divergence is recorded in the report's open question for the PM, and the code comment and changeset state it.

## Tests (HEAD `e7e32f4f`)

- `packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/two-factor-totp-issuer.test.ts` (new, real better-auth pipeline through `AuthManager.handleRequest`, on the in-memory engine the sibling 2FA suites use):
  - the configured app name is the issuer and the label prefix on `enable`, and `ObjectStack` when unset;
  - `get-totp-uri` names the same issuer for the same secret;
  - a branding override set before the instance is built outranks the configured name;
  - **still-works:** an enrollment made under the `Better Auth` label and confirmed is then served by a process configured as `Acme Ops` over the same store. The codes from the OLD URI's secret complete a sign-in challenge, and `get-totp-uri` returns the same secret relabelled. The stored row does not contain the label.
- `packages/cli/src/commands/serve-auth-app-name.contract.test.ts` (new, unit tier):
  - `resolveDeploymentAppName` equals the email chain's answer on all five rungs;
  - a comment-masked scan of `serve.ts` finds exactly one `new AuthPlugin(` call, passing `appName: resolveDeploymentAppName(...)` with the same argument text as the one `resolveEmailCapabilityArg(...)` call.
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/plugin-auth exec vitest run --maxWorkers=2`: 119 files, 2509 passed, 10 skipped.
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/plugin-auth typecheck`: exit 0. It includes `check:test-typecheck`, and the new file compiles clean, with no ledger entry.
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/cli exec vitest run --project unit --maxWorkers=2`: 258 files, 3777 passed. The integration tier is left to CI, because the diff touches no spawn entry and no integration-tier file.
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/cli typecheck`: exit 0.

## Ablations (each through `scripts/ablation-replace.mjs`, restore proven blob == HEAD)

- `auth-manager.ts` without the `appName` line: all 5 new plugin-auth tests turn red, for example `expected { labelIssuer: 'Better Auth', ... } to match object { labelIssuer: 'Acme Ops', ... }`. Restored to blob `a6696db0`, which equals HEAD.
- `serve.ts` without the `AuthPlugin` `appName` line: the construction scan turns red (`AuthPlugin must receive appName from resolveDeploymentAppName: expected +0 to be 1`). Restored to blob `121c8125`, which equals HEAD.
- The same `serve.ts` mutation was rebuilt into `packages/cli/dist` and booted (`ablation-dist-preflight --absent` passed). The result is the `ObjectStack` row in the first table. The restore leg rebuilt `dist` and the preflight found the marker present again, with a clean tree.

## Gates

`node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --commands --repo objectstack-ai/objectstack` derived 99 commands from this branch, and every one exited 0. `--ran` reports: 99 derived, 99 run, 0 NOT-MEASURED, 0 UNRUN. ESLint (`--no-inline-config`) on the 4 changed TS files reports 0 errors and 0 warnings. That run covers only the changed files. `eslint.config.mjs` lints `**/*.{ts,...}` and never enables type-aware linting, so this diff cannot move a verdict on an untouched file.

## Acceptance notes

- `AuthPluginOptions` does not declare `appName`, although `AuthPlugin` forwards it to `AuthManager` by spread. `serve` imports the plugin through a variable specifier, so the call is untyped. A typed host writing `new AuthPlugin({ appName })` gets a loud excess-property error, not a silent drop. Declaring it would widen a published type, so it is left out of this PR, which is `Clause-②: no`. Carrier: none.
- Watch item for a better-auth upgrade: if a later version makes the cookie prefix default from `appName`, as its type doc already claims, the `appName` passed here would rename session cookies on upgrade. Re-check `dist/cookies` when bumping. Carrier: whoever bumps better-auth.
- `plugin-dev` and the `verify` harness construct `AuthPlugin` without `appName`. Neither reads `OS_APP_NAME` anywhere, so no surface there disagrees with another. Noted only.
- `/two-factor/enable` accepts a request-body `issuer` (vendor behaviour, first term above). It only relabels the caller's own enrollment and is display-only. Noted only.
